title: Plantation and Horticulture Part 2 Mock Test

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of cold storage in post-harvest handling?

options.a: To completely stop the respiration of fruits and vegetables
options.b: To maintain low temperatures and slow down spoilage
options.c: To dry the produce for long-term storage
options.d: To increase the sugar content in fruits

questions.explanation: Cold storage helps preserve the freshness of fruits and vegetables by reducing respiration rates, microbial activity, and enzymatic processes.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which type of banana sucker is best for propagation?
questions.explanation: Sword suckers have a strong root system, grow vigorously, and ensure high-yielding banana plants, making them ideal for commercial cultivation.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common method of propagating pineapple (Ananas comosus)?
questions.explanation: Pineapple is propagated vegetatively using suckers, slips, and crowns because seeds are not commonly used due to their long germination period and genetic variability.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the structure at the top of the pineapple fruit that can be used for propagation?
questions.explanation: The crown (leafy top of the fruit) can be removed and planted to grow a new pineapple plant.[cite: 18]

questions.question: How long does it take for a pineapple plant to produce fruit after planting a sucker?
questions.explanation: Pineapple plants grown from suckers take approximately 16-18 months to bear fruit, while crowns take longer (up to 24 months).[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is a rhizome?

options.a: A type of root that stores food
options.b: An underground stem that grows horizontally
options.c: A seed structure used for reproduction
options.d: A type of flower that produces seeds
options.e: A stem that climbs and produces aerial roots

questions.explanation: A rhizome is a specialized underground stem that grows horizontally, giving rise to new shoots and roots.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following plants is propagated through rhizomes?
questions.explanation: Banana is propagated through rhizomes (sword suckers), as it does not produce viable seeds.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of propagating plants through rhizomes?

options.b: It is a slow method of propagation
options.e: It depends on pollination for reproduction

questions.explanation: Rhizomes enable rapid vegetative reproduction, ensuring that new plants are genetically identical to the parent plant.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which part of the turmeric plant (Curcuma longa) is used for propagation?
questions.explanation: Turmeric is propagated by dividing rhizomes, which store food and contain buds that sprout into new plants.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a rhizome-propagated plant?
questions.explanation: Potato is propagated by tubers, not rhizomes. Rhizomes are underground stems, while tubers are swollen underground stems with stored nutrients.[cite: 18]

questions.question: How is Amorphophallus (Elephant Foot Yam) primarily propagated?
questions.explanation: Amorphophallus is propagated by corms, which are underground swollen stems that store food and develop into new plants.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which underground structure is used for propagating Colocasia (Taro)?
questions.explanation: Colocasia is propagated using corms, which are thickened underground stems with buds that sprout into new plants.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following plants is NOT propagated by corms?
questions.explanation: Potato is propagated by tubers, while Gladiolus, Colocasia, and Amorphophallus are propagated by corms.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is a stolon?

options.b: A horizontal stem that grows above or just below the soil
options.c: A swollen underground stem for food storage
options.d: A type of root that stores nutrients
options.e: A modified leaf used for reproduction

questions.explanation: A stolon is a specialized stem that spreads horizontally, producing new plants at nodes when they touch the soil.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following plants is propagated by stolons?
questions.explanation: Strawberry propagates through stolons, which are horizontal stems that spread along the ground and form new plants at nodes.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is a stem tuber?

options.a: A modified root that stores food
options.b: A swollen underground stem that stores nutrients
options.c: A horizontal stem that spreads above ground
options.d: A seed-bearing structure used for reproduction
options.e: A climbing stem used for support

questions.explanation: A stem tuber is an underground storage organ formed from a swollen stem that contains buds (eyes) capable of sprouting into new plants.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What are the small buds on a potato tuber called?
questions.explanation: The "eyes" of a potato tuber are small buds that sprout into new shoots, helping in vegetative propagation.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the main function of a stem tuber?
questions.explanation: Stem tubers store nutrients that help the plant survive unfavorable conditions and enable vegetative propagation through buds (eyes).[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following flowering plants is propagated by tuberous roots?
questions.explanation: Dahlia is propagated using tuberous roots, which store food and develop adventitious buds to grow into new plants.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following flowers is NOT propagated by tuberous roots?
questions.explanation: Gladiolus propagates using corms, not tuberous roots, whereas Dahlia and Begonia use tuberous roots.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which vegetative propagation method is used for Dahlia?
questions.explanation: Dahlia is propagated by dividing its tuberous roots, which develop new shoots from adventitious buds.[cite: 18]

questions.question: In which planting system are trees planted at equal distances in rows and columns?
questions.explanation: The square system arranges trees at equal distances in both directions, forming a grid-like pattern.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which planting system provides the highest number of plants per unit area?
questions.explanation: The hexagonal system accommodates more trees per unit area compared to other systems.[cite: 18]

questions.question: In which planting system is an extra tree planted in the center of each square?
questions.explanation: The quincunx system places a filler tree in the center of each square, maximizing land utilization.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which planting system is most suitable for sloped and hilly areas?
questions.explanation: The contour system follows natural land slopes to prevent soil erosion and water runoff, making it ideal for hilly areas.[cite: 18]

questions.question: In which planting system are trees arranged in a way that each tree is surrounded by six other trees?
questions.explanation: The hexagonal system arranges trees in a honeycomb pattern, ensuring maximum land use and better light distribution.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of training in horticultural plants?

options.b: To control the shape, size, and direction of plant growth

questions.explanation: Training is a technique used to guide plant growth in a specific direction to improve structure and productivity.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What does pruning primarily involve?
questions.explanation: Pruning is the careful removal of branches, leaves, or other parts to improve plant health, flowering, and fruit production.[cite: 18]

questions.question: How does pruning benefit plants?

options.b: Improves flowering, fruitfulness, and fruit quality

questions.explanation: Pruning helps direct energy to fruiting and flowering, improving yield and overall plant health.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE about training?

options.a: It reduces the need for irrigation
options.b: It controls the shape, size, and direction of plant growth
options.c: It is only done on herbaceous plants
options.e: It increases the number of leaves

questions.explanation: Training guides plant growth for better structural strength, ease of management, and improved productivity.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the main difference between training and pruning?

options.a: Training is a growth technique, while pruning is a removal technique
options.b: Training removes plant parts, while pruning controls growth
options.c: Training prevents disease, while pruning promotes disease
options.d: Training increases plant stress, while pruning reduces stress
options.e: Training is only for flowers, while pruning is only for fruits

questions.explanation: Training helps shape the plant's growth, while pruning removes unwanted parts to improve health and productivity.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of nipping (pinching) in plants?

options.b: To promote lateral branching and bushy growth
options.d: To reduce the need for irrigation

questions.explanation: Nipping removes the apical dominance, encouraging the plant to develop more side branches, resulting in a bushier structure.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Nipping is mainly performed on which part of the plant?
questions.explanation: Nipping involves pinching off the soft growing tips to stimulate lateral bud growth and branching.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following crops commonly benefits from nipping?
questions.explanation: Nipping in cotton promotes more branches, increasing flowering and yield.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is de-shooting in plants?

options.b: Removing flowers to promote vegetative growth
options.c: Cutting the roots to control plant height
options.d: Removing lateral buds to encourage a single main stem

questions.explanation: De-shooting is the practice of removing lateral buds to direct plant energy into a single strong stem, producing larger flowers.[cite: 18]

questions.question: De-shooting is most effective in which type of plant growth?
questions.explanation: De-shooting is used in flowering plants grown for large blooms, such as Chrysanthemum and Dahlia.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is topiary?

options.a: A method of pruning plants into decorative shapes
options.b: A technique for increasing plant height
options.d: A technique for grafting fruit trees
options.e: A way to improve plant nutrition

questions.explanation: Topiary is the art of training and pruning plants into ornamental shapes such as animals, geometric figures, or objects.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the Open Center (Vase Shape) system in plant training?

options.a: A method of planting trees in rows
options.b: A technique of allowing multiple main branches from a short trunk
options.c: A system of grafting plants for better yield
options.d: A method of pruning to increase plant height
options.e: A method of planting in a circular pattern

questions.explanation: In the Open Center system, the central leader is removed, and 3-5 main branches grow outward, creating a vase-like shape.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following fruit crops is commonly trained using the Open Center system?
questions.explanation: Peach, Plum, Apricot, and other stone fruits are commonly trained in the Open Center system to allow sunlight penetration and air circulation.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the Central Leader System in plant training?

options.a: A method where the central stem is removed for bushy growth
options.b: A technique where a single dominant trunk is maintained with lateral branches
options.c: A method of planting trees in rows for high density
options.d: A system of pruning used only for shrubs
options.e: A method of training climbing plants

questions.explanation: In the Central Leader System, a single strong trunk (leader) is maintained, and lateral branches grow around it, creating a conical or pyramidal shape.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following fruit trees is commonly trained using the Central Leader System?
questions.explanation: Apple, Pear, and other pome fruits are commonly trained using the Central Leader System to promote strong vertical growth.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What shape does a tree trained in the Central Leader System typically have?
questions.explanation: Trees trained using the Central Leader System have a conical or pyramid-like structure, with a dominant central trunk and evenly spaced lateral branches.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the Modified Leader System in plant training?

options.a: A system where a single trunk is maintained throughout the tree's life
options.b: A combination of the Central Leader and Open Center systems
options.c: A method used only for vines and creepers
options.d: A system that does not involve pruning
options.e: A planting method used for root vegetables

questions.explanation: The Modified Leader System starts with a strong central trunk, but after a few years, the central leader is pruned, allowing multiple scaffold branches to develop, similar to the Open Center system.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following fruits is NOT typically grown using the Cordon or Trellis System?
questions.explanation: Mango trees are large and not suitable for the Cordon System, which is mostly used for vines and small fruiting plants.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following crops is most commonly trained using the Cordon or Trellis System?
questions.explanation: Grapevines are commonly trained using the Cordon System to maximize fruit exposure to sunlight and improve yield.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the Cordon System in plant training?

options.a: A method where trees are allowed to grow naturally without pruning
options.b: A training system where plants are grown with a single or multiple stems supported by a structure
options.c: A planting technique used for tuber crops
options.d: A method of irrigation for fruit trees
options.e: A technique used for soil improvement

questions.explanation: The Cordon System is used to train plants in a controlled manner along a support system like a trellis, fence, or wires.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What type of structure is commonly used in the Cordon or Trellis System?
questions.explanation: Plants in the Cordon or Trellis System are trained along horizontal supports like wires, stakes, or fences for better management and yield.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is pruning in horticulture?

options.a: A method of planting trees in rows
options.b: The judicious removal of plant parts to influence growth and improve quality
options.c: A technique used only for flowering plants
options.d: A system of irrigation used in fruit orchards
options.e: The removal of soil around the roots to enhance growth

questions.explanation: Pruning is done to remove unwanted plant parts, improve air circulation, increase fruit quality, and shape the plant.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the primary objective of pruning fruit trees?
questions.explanation: Pruning helps remove excess branches, allowing more energy to be directed toward fruit production, improving size and quality.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the best time for pruning most deciduous fruit trees?

options.c: During the dormant season (late winter or early spring)

questions.explanation: Pruning in the dormant season allows plants to heal before the growing season begins, reducing stress and improving growth.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which type of pruning involves the removal of an entire branch from its point of origin?
questions.explanation: Thinning out removes an entire branch from its base, improving air circulation and reducing overcrowding.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the term for the removal of young shoot tips to encourage bushy growth?
questions.explanation: Pinching removes the shoot tip, encouraging lateral branching and a bushier appearance in plants.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which fruit crop benefits the most from heavy pruning?
questions.explanation: Grapevines require heavy annual pruning to maintain fruiting wood and control excessive vegetative growth.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a plant that benefits from heading back pruning?
questions.explanation: Roses are commonly pruned using heading back to promote bushy growth and more flowering.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is heading back in pruning?

options.a: Removing an entire branch from its point of origin
options.b: Cutting back a part of a branch to a bud or lateral shoot
options.c: Removing only dried leaves from a plant

questions.explanation: Heading back is a pruning technique that shortens branches to promote bushier growth and encourage lateral shoots.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is dehorning in pruning?

options.a: The removal of small twigs and leaves from a tree
options.b: The drastic removal of large, mature branches to rejuvenate an old tree
options.c: The cutting of flowers before they bloom
options.d: A method of preventing plant diseases
options.e: A process used only in vegetable crops

questions.explanation: Dehorning is a severe pruning method used to rejuvenate old or unproductive trees by cutting back large branches.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which type of pruning is used for rejuvenating old, unproductive fruit trees?
questions.explanation: Dehorning is a drastic pruning method where large branches are removed to stimulate new growth in old fruit trees.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which type of pruning involves cutting back a portion of a branch to a bud or lateral shoot to encourage bushy growth?
questions.explanation: Heading back stimulates lateral growth and makes plants bushier, commonly used in fruit trees and ornamental shrubs.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which type of pruning is commonly practiced in bonsai plants?
questions.explanation: Root pruning helps maintain small plant size, making it essential in bonsai cultivation.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of frame pruning?

options.a: To shape the plant by removing weak and unproductive branches
options.b: To remove excess flower buds for better fruit quality
options.c: To cut the roots and limit plant growth
options.d: To remove large, mature branches for rejuvenation

questions.explanation: Frame pruning is used to develop a strong framework in plants by removing weak branches, ensuring better structure and productivity.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the main objective of maintenance pruning?

options.a: To drastically reduce the height of the plant
options.b: To remove diseased, dead, or weak branches and maintain the plant's shape
options.d: To completely stop flowering and fruiting
options.e: To cut off all side branches for a single-stem structure

questions.explanation: Maintenance pruning helps in keeping plants healthy by removing damaged parts and ensuring proper structure and air circulation.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of ringing or girdling in plants?

options.a: To remove excess leaves and branches
options.b: To stimulate flowering and fruiting by disrupting the downward flow of food (phloem)
options.c: To completely kill the plant for replanting
options.d: To increase vegetative growth by cutting roots
options.e: To prevent water loss during drought conditions

questions.explanation: Ringing (girdling) involves removing a strip of bark from a branch or trunk, temporarily blocking the downward movement of carbohydrates, which helps in improving flowering and fruiting.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the best season for notching in fig plants?
questions.explanation: Notching in fig is best done during August-September, as this helps in stimulating lateral bud growth and improving fruit production.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the main objective of notching in horticultural crops?

options.b: To increase water absorption by roots
options.c: To stimulate lateral bud development and improve branching
options.d: To reduce fruit size for better quality

questions.explanation: Notching helps break apical dominance by making small cuts above a bud, encouraging new shoot formation.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following practices are done to induce flowering and fruiting in horticulture plants?
questions.explanation: Pruning, root pruning, ringing, girdling, notching, bending, smudging are some of the specialized horticultural practices followed for regulation of fruiting.[cite: 18]

questions.question: ___ is the common practice in Maharashtra to induce flowering in guava
questions.explanation: Bending a branch downward, sometimes checks growth and causes accumulation of starch in the branch with greater flowering. This tends to increase carbohydrate concentration. This is usually practiced with local guava variety in the Maharashtra state (Deccan area).[cite: 18]

questions.question: What happens physiologically when a notch is made above a bud in a plant?

options.a: It enhances the downward movement of auxins
options.b: It restricts auxin flow, promoting lateral bud growth
options.d: It prevents photosynthesis in the leaves

questions.explanation: Notching blocks auxin movement, reducing apical dominance and stimulating lateral shoot growth.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Smudging is most commonly used in which fruit crop?
questions.explanation: Smudging is widely used in mango orchards to induce flowering, especially in regions where natural flowering is delayed due to low temperatures.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of smudging in horticulture?

options.c: To induce early flowering and fruiting by producing smoke
options.d: To reduce water loss from leaves
options.e: To remove unwanted branches from trees

questions.explanation: Smudging is a technique where smoke is generated around trees, primarily in mango orchards, to create a warmer microclimate and stimulate flowering.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Root pruning is generally practiced in which horticulture plants to induce flowering and fruiting?
questions.explanation: Root pruning results in less carbohydrate utilization of the top growth through there is a little more utilization of carbohydrate for root functions. The trees burst into flowering in about 2-3 weeks of root pruning. Practice very widely adopted by citrus growers in western and central India (in santra).[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the purpose of Bahar treatment in horticulture?

options.c: To regulate flowering and fruiting according to market demand

questions.explanation: Bahar treatment is a horticultural practice used in fruit crops like pomegranate and citrus to control the timing of flowering and fruiting for better yield and market availability.[cite: 18]

questions.question: In Bahar treatment, which of the following seasons corresponds to flowering in June-July?
questions.explanation: Mrig Bahar flowering occurs in June-July, leading to fruit harvest in winter. It is commonly practiced in areas with sufficient monsoon rains.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Hasta Bahar flowering occurs in which months?
questions.explanation: Hasta Bahar flowering occurs in October-November, with fruit harvesting in summer. This is useful in areas where water availability is sufficient during fruit development.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Ambe Bahar flowering is induced during which season?
questions.explanation: Ambe Bahar flowering occurs in winter (December-February), with fruits maturing in monsoon (June-July). This is the most preferred season in areas with assured irrigation.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Bahar treatment is commonly practiced in which of the following fruit crops?
questions.explanation: Bahar treatment is mainly used in fruit crops like pomegranate and citrus to regulate flowering and fruiting cycles according to seasonal and market requirements.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the primary objective of Bahar treatment in fruit crops?

options.b: To regulate flowering and fruiting according to season and market demand
options.d: To reduce fruit drop in all seasons

questions.explanation: Bahar treatment is used to control the flowering season in fruit crops like pomegranate and citrus to ensure better yield and market availability.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following growth retardants is commonly used in mango to regulate growth?
questions.explanation: Cycocel (CCC) at 1000 ppm is used in mango to control excessive vegetative growth and promote flowering by reducing gibberellin activity.[cite: 18]

questions.question: In mango, Cycocel (CCC)is applied at what concentration to regulate vegetative growth?
questions.explanation: In mango, Cycocel (CCC) at 1000 ppm is used to control vegetative growth and induce flowering.[cite: 18]

questions.question: The disappearance of angularity is used as a maturity index in which fruit?
questions.explanation: In bananas, the disappearance of angularity (rounding of fingers) indicates maturity and readiness for harvest.[cite: 18]

questions.question: The minimum TSS requirement for grapes at maturity is
questions.explanation: Grapes are considered mature when they have a TSS of 14-17.5%, depending on the cultivar, with a TSS/TA ratio of 20 or higher.[cite: 18]

questions.question: The maturity index of guava is determined by:

options.c: Color break stage (from dark green to light green)
options.e: Disappearance of fuzz on fruit skin

questions.explanation: Guava is harvested at the color break stage when the skin changes from dark green to light green.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the maturity index for brinjal (eggplant)?

options.b: Skin turning from green to yellow
options.c: Immature, glossy skin, harvested 40 days from flowering
options.d: Development of black streaks on fruit surface

questions.explanation: Brinjal is harvested when it has an immature, glossy skin and is about 40 days from flowering.[cite: 18]

questions.question: The recommended maturity index for harvesting potatoes is

options.a: When the tubers reach full size
options.b: Before vines die completely, followed by curing
options.c: When the skin starts turning soft
options.d: At the flowering stage of the plant
options.e: When the leaves begin to curl

questions.explanation: Potatoes are harvested before the vines die completely, and curing is done to heal surface wounds.[cite: 18]

questions.question: The maturity index for tomatoes is

options.a: When the fruit reaches full size
options.b: Seeds fully developed and gel formation advanced in at least one locule
options.c: When the fruit turns completely red
options.d: When the outer skin develops wrinkles
options.e: When the fruit detaches easily from the plant

questions.explanation: Tomatoes are harvested when the seeds are fully developed and gel formation is advanced in at least one locule.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which post-harvest operation is performed to remove dirt, pesticide residues, and microbial contaminants from produce?
questions.explanation: Washing helps remove soil, chemicals, and pathogens from fruits and vegetables to maintain hygiene and quality.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary objective of post-harvest handling operations?

options.a: To increase the weight of produce
options.b: To reduce water content in fruits
options.c: To maintain quality, extend shelf life, and minimize losses
options.d: To enhance plant growth after harvesting
options.e: To make fruits and vegetables look attractive only

questions.explanation: Post-harvest handling operations aim to preserve freshness, minimize spoilage, and extend the marketability of fruits and vegetables.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the purpose of grading in post-harvest handling?

options.b: To sort produce based on size, shape, color, and quality
options.c: To dry the produce for longer storage

questions.explanation: Grading ensures uniformity in quality and appearance, making it easier for consumers and markets to accept the produce.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which method is commonly used to extend the shelf life of fruits by reducing water loss and respiration?
questions.explanation: Waxing forms a protective layer on the surface of fruits like apples, citrus, and cucumbers to reduce water loss and delay aging.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the main purpose of pre-cooling in post-harvest handling?

options.a: To increase the temperature of harvested produce
options.b: To remove field heat and slow down respiration
options.c: To kill pathogens in fruits and vegetables
options.e: To improve the color of vegetables

questions.explanation: Pre-cooling helps in maintaining quality by reducing temperature and slowing down respiration rates.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following is a common storage method for perishable fruits and vegetables?
questions.explanation: Cold storage slows down ripening, reduces microbial growth, and extends the shelf life of perishable produce.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Modified Atmosphere Packaging (MAP) is used in post-harvest handling to

options.b: Reduce the rate of respiration and delay ripening
options.c: Remove ethylene gas from storage rooms

questions.explanation: MAP alters oxygen and carbon dioxide levels to slow down respiration and extend the freshness of produce.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a post-harvest treatment used for extending the shelf life of fruits?
questions.explanation: Artificial coloring is not a recommended post-harvest treatment for fresh produce as it does not help in preserving quality[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which storage technique is used for climacteric fruits like bananas and mangoes to control ripening?
questions.explanation: CAS adjusts oxygen, carbon dioxide, and ethylene levels to control ripening and extend the storage life of climacteric fruits.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of removing field heat from harvested produce?

options.a: To enhance the color of fruits
options.c: To slow down respiration and reduce spoilage
options.d: To increase the weight of produce
options.e: To make the produce softer for packing

questions.explanation: Field heat removal helps in preserving freshness, delaying ripening, and reducing microbial growth.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following methods is commonly used for removing field heat from freshly harvested fruits and vegetables?
questions.explanation: Pre-cooling rapidly removes heat from produce, reducing respiration and maintaining quality.[cite: 18]

questions.question: In which pre-cooling method is freshly harvested produce immersed in cold water to remove field heat?
questions.explanation: Hydro-cooling involves submerging or spraying produce with chilled water to quickly reduce its temperature.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of grading in post-harvest handling of fruits and vegetables?

options.a: To increase the weight of produce artificially
options.b: To sort produce based on size, shape, color, and quality
options.c: To speed up the ripening process
options.d: To remove moisture content from produce

questions.explanation: Grading ensures uniformity, enhances market value, and improves consumer acceptance by categorizing produce based on quality parameters.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which of the following pre-cooling methods is most effective for leafy vegetables?
questions.explanation: Vacuum cooling is ideal for leafy greens as it rapidly cools the produce by evaporating moisture under low pressure.[cite: 18]

questions.question: Which pre-cooling method involves placing harvested produce in a cold storage room to gradually lower its temperature?
questions.explanation: Room cooling is a slow but effective method where produce is kept in a cold storage room to gradually reduce its temperature.[cite: 18]

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using Modified Atmosphere Packaging (MAP) for fruits and vegetables?

options.a: It increases oxygen levels to accelerate ripening
options.b: It reduces respiration rate and extends shelf life
options.c: It adds artificial flavors to improve taste
options.d: It removes all moisture from the produce
options.e: It exposes produce to direct sunlight for preservation

questions.explanation: Modified Atmosphere Packaging (MAP) alters the levels of gases (O2, CO2 and N2 around the produce, slowing down respiration and spoilage.[cite: 18]
